examples.en: My child says he wants to go to the moon.
There's a story that rabbits live on the moon.
What would it be like to travel to the moon by spaceship?
I read a story about the moon world in a picture book.

examples.ko: 어릴 때는 달나라가 정말 있는 줄 알았어요.
examples.en: When I was little, I thought a moon world really existed.
In the children's song, cassia trees grow in the moon world.

explain: 동화나 동요, 아이들과 하는 이야기에서 달을 하나의 나라처럼 부르는 말이에요. 과학 이야기에서는 그냥 '달'이라고 해요. '달님'과 함께 아이들 말투에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It treats the moon like a country, and is used in fairy tales, children's songs and talk with kids. In scientific contexts people just say '달'. It sounds childlike, like '달님'.

examples.en: I go to a dance class every weekend.
That singer's dancing is really cool.

examples.ko: 댄스 연습 때문에 매일 늦게 집에 와요.
examples.en: Because of dance practice I come home late every day.
I am learning dance together with a friend.
This is a dance track, so it is fun.
Dance videos are very popular these days.

explain: '춤'이 원래 쓰던 우리말이고, '댄스'는 학원 이름이나 '댄스곡', '댄스 가수'처럼 합성어에서 자주 나와요. 동사는 '춤을 추다'라고 해야 하고 '댄스를 추다'는 어색해요. '방송 댄스', '재즈 댄스'처럼 종류 이름에도 댄스를 써요.
explain_en: 춤 is the native word, while 댄스 shows up in compounds like 댄스곡 and 댄스 가수, and in class names. For the verb you must say 춤을 추다; 댄스를 추다 sounds off. 댄스 is also used in genre names such as 재즈 댄스.

dis.h: loanword for dance; pop or studio style

p.n: Both work; 댄스 sounds more like a class or trend.

examples.en: Mom massages Dad's shoulders.
I massaged my legs after exercising.
If you get a massage every day, your fatigue goes away.
I bought a face-massage device.
My neck hurts, so I'm going for a massage.
Drink plenty of water after a massage.

explain: 가게에서는 보통 '마사지를 받다'라고 하고, 직접 하거나 해 줄 때는 '마사지하다'를 써요. 집에서 가족끼리 어깨를 풀어 줄 때는 '주물러 주다'를 더 자주 말해요. 몸을 풀어 주는 예전부터 쓰던 말은 '안마'이고, '안마 의자'처럼 써요.
explain_en: At a shop you usually say '마사지를 받다' (get a massage), and '마사지하다' is for doing it yourself or giving one. For family loosening each other's shoulders at home, '주물러 주다' (to knead) is more common. The older Korean word for it is '안마', as in '안마 의자' (massage chair).

p.n: 안마 is more about relieving tired muscles by hand.

en: playing in the water; water play

examples.en: In summer I go play in the water with my family.

examples.ko: 수영장에서 물놀이를 하기 전에 준비 운동을 해요.
examples.en: I warm up before playing in the water at the pool.
The weather is great for playing in the water today.
It rained, so we couldn't play in the water.
Be sure to bring a tube when you go play in the water.
After playing in the water, I take a shower with warm water.

explain: 수영처럼 실력을 보여 주는 운동이 아니라 계곡, 바다, 수영장에서 물에 들어가 노는 것을 말해요. '물놀이를 하다/가다'로 많이 써요. '사물놀이'와 소리가 비슷하지만 전혀 다른 말이에요.
explain_en: Unlike swimming as exercise, it is about getting into water at a valley, beach or pool just to play. It is often used as '물놀이를 하다/가다'. It sounds a bit like '사물놀이', but that is a completely different word.

examples.en: This channel broadcasts news 24 hours a day.

examples.ko: 오늘 저녁 일곱 시에 경기를 방송할 거예요.
examples.en: They will broadcast the game at seven this evening.

examples.ko: 그 방송국은 매주 토요일 밤에 드라마를 방송하고 있어요.
examples.en: That broadcaster airs a drama every Saturday night.

examples.ko: 어제 라디오에서 그 가수의 인터뷰를 방송했어요.
examples.en: The radio aired that singer's interview yesterday.

examples.ko: 동생은 집에서 게임하는 모습을 인터넷으로 방송하려고 해요.
examples.en: My younger brother plans to stream himself playing games at home.
The show that's on right now is really fun.

explain: '방송하다'는 방송국이나 채널이 주어일 때 써요. 프로그램이 주어이면 '방송되다'를 써서 '드라마가 방송돼요'라고 해요. 일상에서는 '오늘 몇 시에 해요?'처럼 짧게 묻는 일이 많고, 인터넷으로 영상을 내보내는 것도 '방송하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: '방송하다' takes a station or channel as its subject; when a program is the subject, use the passive '방송되다' ('드라마가 방송돼요'). In daily talk people just ask '오늘 몇 시에 해요?' (What time is it on today?). Streaming online is also called '방송하다'.

dis.h: broadcast on TV or radio, any content

p.n: 방영하다 is for airing shows or films, so it does not fit radio news.

examples.en: There are two apple trees in the garden.

examples.ko: 가을이 되면 사과나무에 빨간 사과가 열려요.
examples.en: In autumn, red apples grow on the apple tree.
Grandfather is watering the apple tree.
We ate our lunch under the apple tree.
Apple trees bloom with white flowers in spring.

examples.ko: 농장에서 사과나무를 직접 보고 사과를 땄어요.
examples.en: At the farm I saw the apple trees up close and picked apples.

explain: 과일 나무는 보통 열매 이름 뒤에 '나무'를 붙여요(배나무, 감나무, 사과나무). 나무는 '그루'로 세어서 '사과나무 한 그루'라고 해요. 열매는 '열리다', 꽃은 '피다'를 써요.
explain_en: Fruit trees are usually named by adding 나무 to the fruit (배나무, 감나무, 사과나무). Trees are counted with 그루: '사과나무 한 그루'. Fruit uses 열리다 and flowers use 피다.

examples.en: I ate raw sliced fish by the sea on the weekend.
The fresher the raw fish is here, the better it tastes.
Try dipping the raw fish in spicy red pepper sauce.

examples.ko: 저는 생선회를 못 먹어서 구이를 시켰어요.
examples.en: I can't eat raw fish, so I ordered grilled fish.

examples.ko: 이 식당은 생선회 한 접시에 얼마예요?
examples.en: How much is one plate of raw fish at this restaurant?

examples.ko: 생선회랑 같이 나오는 매운탕도 정말 맛있어요.
examples.en: The spicy fish stew that comes with the raw fish is really good too.

explain: 보통은 줄여서 '회'라고 많이 말해요. '회를 먹다', '회를 뜨다'처럼 쓰고, 식당에서도 '회 한 접시 주세요'라고 하면 자연스러워요. 상추나 깻잎에 싸 먹거나 초고추장, 쌈장과 함께 먹는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: People often shorten it to just '회'. You say '회를 먹다' (eat raw fish) or '회를 뜨다' (slice raw fish), and at a restaurant '회 한 접시 주세요' sounds natural. It is often wrapped in lettuce or perilla leaves, or eaten with spicy red pepper sauce or ssamjang.

examples.en: This winter there is more snow than last year.
The cold this winter is severe, and the water pipes froze.
This winter I want to try learning to ski.
I bought a padded jacket in advance for this winter.
I'm worried about how big the heating bill will be this winter.

examples.ko: 올겨울이 끝나면 새집으로 이사를 갈 거예요.
examples.en: When this winter is over, we're going to move to a new house.

explain: '올해 겨울'을 줄인 말이고, 지금 겨울이거나 곧 올 겨울을 가리켜요. 지난해 겨울은 '지난겨울'이라고 해요. '올봄, 올여름, 올가을'과 같은 방식으로 쓰는 말이에요.
explain_en: It is a shortened '올해 겨울' and points to the winter happening now or coming soon. Last year's winter is '지난겨울'. It follows the same pattern as '올봄', '올여름' and '올가을'.

examples.en: The reporter interviews a famous singer.
I'm going to interview people from the company tomorrow.
I interviewed a teacher for the school newspaper.
I prepared my questions before the interview.

examples.ko: 그 배우를 직접 만나서 인터뷰하고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to meet that actor in person and interview him.
I organized what I got from the interview and wrote an article.

explain: 취업 면접은 보통 '인터뷰'가 아니라 '면접'이라고 하고, '면접을 보다'처럼 '보다'와 같이 써요. '인터뷰하다'는 기자나 조사하는 사람이 묻는 쪽일 때 어울리고, 상대는 '을/를'로 받아요. 대답하는 쪽은 '인터뷰에 응하다'라고 해요.
explain_en: A job interview is usually called '면접', used with '보다' ('면접을 보다'), not 인터뷰. 인터뷰하다 fits a reporter or researcher doing the asking, and the person asked takes the particle 을/를. The person answering 'accepts the interview', '인터뷰에 응하다'.

examples.en: The midterms start next week.
Because of the midterms, I study until late at night these days.
The day before the midterm, there are no seats in the library.
My math score went up on this midterm.
I did well on the midterm, so my parents were happy.
There are no club meetings during midterm period.

explain: 학기 중간에 보는 시험이 중간고사이고, 학기 끝에 보는 시험은 '기말고사'예요. '시험을 보다'처럼 '중간고사를 보다'라고 말해요. '중간고사를 치르다'는 글에서 더 많이 보여요.
explain_en: The exam in the middle of a term is the 중간고사 and the one at the end is the 기말고사. Say '중간고사를 보다', like '시험을 보다'; '중간고사를 치르다' appears more in writing.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 한 번 플레이 시간이 짧아요.
examples.en: This game has a short play time per round.

examples.ko: 선수들이 오늘 멋진 플레이를 보여 줬어요.
examples.en: The players showed great play today.
The first play is easy, but it gets harder as you go.

examples.ko: 오늘 경기에서는 팀 플레이가 아주 좋았어요.
examples.en: The teamwork was very good in today's match.

examples.ko: 친구랑 같이 게임 플레이 영상을 봤어요.
examples.en: I watched a gameplay video with a friend.
When the play ends, the score shows right away.

explain: 스포츠와 게임에서 선수나 게이머가 움직이는 모습을 '플레이'라고 해요. 영상은 '재생'이 더 흔해서 '재생 버튼'이라고 말하는 경우가 많아요. '플레이하다'도 있지만 말할 때는 '게임을 하다', '경기를 하다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: In sports and games, 플레이 means how a player moves and performs. For video, 재생 is more common, so people usually say 재생 버튼. 플레이하다 exists, but in speech 게임을 하다 and 경기를 하다 sound more natural.

dis.h: English loanword for playing a game

p.n: 놀이 does not combine naturally with 게임 here.
